arxiv-2111-02194.title: Learning Implicit Sentiment in Aspect-based Sentiment Analysis with Supervised Contrastive Pre-Training
arxiv-2111-02194.creator: Zhengyan Li, Yicheng Zou, Chong Zhang, Qi Zhang, Zhongyu Wei
arxiv-2111-02194.description: Abstract Aspect-based sentiment analysis aims to identify the sentiment polarity of a specific aspect in product reviews. We notice that about 30% of reviews do not contain obvious opinion words, but still convey clear human-aware sentiment orientation, which is known as implicit sentiment. However, recent neural network-based approaches paid little attention to implicit sentiment entailed in the reviews.

arxiv-2206-14222.title: Deconfined Quantum Critical Point with Non-locality
arxiv-2206-14222.creator: Yichen Xu, Xiao-Chuan Wu, Cenke Xu
arxiv-2206-14222.description: Abstract The deconfined quantum critical point (DQCP) between the Néel and valence bond solid (VBS) order was originally proposed in quantum spin systems with a local Hamiltonian. In the last few years analogues of DQCPs with nonlocal interactions have been explored, which can lead to rich possibilities.

arxiv-2210-03490.title: On the normality of monoid monomorphisms Thanks: This work is supported by Fundação para a Ciência e a Tecnologia FCT/MCTES (PIDDAC) through the following Projects: Associate Laboratory ARISE LA/P/0112/2020; UIDP/04044/2020; UIDB/04044/2020; PAMI - ROTEIRO/0328/2013 (Nº 022158); MATIS (CENTRO-01-014
arxiv-2210-03490.creator: Nelson Martins-Ferreira, Manuela Sobral
arxiv-2210-03490.description: Abstract . In the category of monoids we characterize monomorphisms that are normal, in an appropriate sense, to internal reflexive relations, preorders or equivalence relations. The zero-classes of such internal relations are first described in terms of convenient syntactic relations associated to them and then through the adjunctions associated with the corresponding normalization functors.

arxiv-2302-03168.title: Multiplicity of northern bright O-type stars with optical long baseline interferometry
arxiv-2302-03168.creator: C. Lanthermann, J.-B. Le Bouquin, H. Sana, A. Mérand, J. D. Monnier, K. Perraut, A.J. Frost, L. Mahy, E. Gosset, M. De Becker, S. Kraus, N. Anugu, C. L. Davies, J. Ennis, T. Gardner, A. Labdon, B. Setterholm, T. ten Brummelaar, G. H. Schaefer
arxiv-2302-03168.description: Abstract Context. The study of the multiplicity of massive stars gives hints on their formation processes and their evolutionary paths, which are still not fully understood. Large separation binaries (¿50 milliseconds of arc, mas) can be probed by adaptive-optics-assisted direct imaging and sparse aperture masking, while close binaries can be resolved by photometry and spectroscopy.

arxiv-2402-05301.title: BIKED++: A Multimodal Dataset of 1.4 Million Bicycle Image and Parametric CAD Designs
arxiv-2402-05301.creator: Lyle Regenwetter 1 , Yazan Abu Obaideh 2 , Amin Heyrani Nobari 1 , Faez Ahmed 1
arxiv-2402-05301.description: Abstract This paper introduces a public dataset of 1.4 million procedurally-generated bicycle designs represented parametrically, as JSON files, and as rasterized images. The dataset is created through the use of a rendering engine which harnesses the BikeCAD software to generate vector graphics from parametric designs. This rendering engine is discussed in the paper and also released publicly alongside the dataset.

arxiv-2404-14950.title: Sharp quasi-invariance threshold for the cubic Szegő equation
arxiv-2404-14950.creator: James Coe and Leonardo Tolomeo
arxiv-2404-14950.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by James Coe and Leonardo Tolomeo. We consider the 1-dimensional cubic Szegő equation with data distributed according to the Gaussian measure with inverse covariance operator ( 1 − ∂ x 2 ) s (1-\partial_{x}^{2})^{s} , where s > 1 2 s>\frac{1}{2} .

arxiv-2406-13724.title: Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks with Post-hoc Explanations for Multi-modal and Explainable Land Use Inference
arxiv-2406-13724.creator: Xuehao Zhai, Junqi Jiang, Adam Dejl, Antonio Rago, Fangce Guo, Francesca Toni, Aruna Sivakumar
arxiv-2406-13724.description: Abstract Urban land use inference is a critically important task that aids in city planning and policy-making. Recently, the increased use of sensor and location technologies has facilitated the collection of multi-modal mobility data, offering valuable insights into daily activity patterns.

arxiv-2410-08905.title: Lifelong Event Detection via Optimal Transport
arxiv-2410-08905.creator: Viet Dao, Van-Cuong Pham, Quyen Tran, Thanh-Thien Le, Linh Ngo Van, Thien Huu Nguyen
arxiv-2410-08905.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Viet Dao, Van-Cuong Pham, Quyen Tran, Thanh-Thien Le, Linh Ngo Van, Thien Huu Nguyen. Continual Event Detection (CED) poses a formidable challenge due to the catastrophic forgetting phenomenon, where learning new tasks (with new coming event types) hampers performance on previous ones.

arxiv-2503-16385.title: Deconstructing Long Chain-of-Thought: A Structured Reasoning Optimization Framework for Long CoT Distillation
arxiv-2503-16385.creator: Yijia Luo, Yulin Song, Xingyao Zhang, Jiaheng Liu, Weixun Wang, GengRu Chen, Wenbo Su, Bo Zheng
arxiv-2503-16385.description: Abstract Recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable reasoning capabilities through long chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning. The R1 distillation scheme has emerged as a promising approach for training cost-effective models with enhanced reasoning abilities. However, the underlying mechanisms driving its effectiveness remain unclear.

arxiv-2503-20142.title: Local Linear Convergence of the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers for Semidefinite Programming under Strict Complementarity
arxiv-2503-20142.creator: Shucheng Kang, Xin Jiang, Heng Yang
arxiv-2503-20142.description: Abstract We investigate the local linear convergence properties of the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) when applied to Semidefinite Programming (SDP). A longstanding belief suggests that ADMM is only capable of solving SDPs to moderate accuracy, primarily due to its sublinear worst-case complexity and empirical observations of slow convergence.

arxiv-2506-19460.title: The Crab Nebula at subarcsecond resolution with the International LOFAR Telescope
arxiv-2506-19460.creator: M. Arias, R. Timmerman, F. Sweijen, R. J. van Weeren, C. G. Bassa
arxiv-2506-19460.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by M. Arias, R. Timmerman, F. Sweijen, R. J. van Weeren, C. G. Bassa. We present International LOw Frequency ARray (LOFAR) Telescope (ILT) observations of the Crab Nebula, the remnant of a core-collapse supernova explosion observed by astronomers in 1054.

arxiv-2509-11496.title: Notebook for the CheckThat! Lab at CLEF 2025
arxiv-2509-11496.creator: Fabrycio Leite Nakano Almada, Kauan Divino Pouso Mariano, Maykon Adriell Dutra, Victor Emanuel da Silva Monteiro, Juliana Resplande Sant’Anna Gomes, Arlindo Rodrigues Galvão Filho, Anderson da Silva Soares
arxiv-2509-11496.description: Abstract Claim normalization, the transformation of informal social media posts into concise, self-contained statements, is a crucial step in automated fact-checking pipelines. This paper details our submission to the CLEF-2025 CheckThat! Task 2, which challenges systems to perform claim normalization across twenty languages, divided into thirteen supervised (high-resource) and seven zero-shot (no training data) tracks.

pmc-10532023.title: Diagnostic Work-Up in Patients with Nonbacterial Thrombotic Endocarditis
pmc-10532023.creator: Antonio Tonutti, Iside Scarfò, Giovanni La Canna, Carlo Selmi, Maria De Santis, Francesco Pelliccia, Mohammad Reza Movahed
pmc-10532023.description: Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE) is a form of endocarditis that occurs in patients with predisposing conditions, including malignancies, autoimmune diseases (particularly antiphospholipid antibody syndrome, which accounts for the majority of lupus-associated cases), and coagulation disturbances for which the correlation with classical determinants is unclear.

pmc-11474423.title: Predicting mortality in febrile adults: comparative performance of the MEWS, qSOFA, and UVA scores using prospectively collected data among patients in four health-care sites in sub-Saharan Africa and South-Eastern Asia
pmc-11474423.creator: Sham Lal, Manophab Luangraj, Suzanne H Keddie, Elizabeth A Ashley, Oliver Baerenbold, Quique Bassat, John Bradley, John A Crump, Nicholas A Feasey, Edward W Green, Kevin C Kain, Ioana D Olaru, David G Lalloo, Chrissy h Roberts, David CW Mabey, Christopher C Moore, Heidi Hopkins, the Febrile Illness
pmc-11474423.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). SummaryBackgroundClinical severity scores can identify patients at risk of severe disease and death, and improve patient management. The modified early warning score (MEWS), the quick Sequential (Sepsis-Related) Organ Failure Assessment (qSOFA), and the Universal Vital Assessment (UVA) were developed as risk-stratification tools, but they have not been fully validated in low-resource settings where fever and infectious diseases are frequent reasons for health care seeking.

pmc-11643953.title: Impact of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus on Fetal Growth and Nutritional Status in Newborns
pmc-11643953.creator: Karolina Karcz, Barbara Królak-Olejnik, Blessing J Akombi-Inyang
pmc-11643953.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is one of the most prevalent complications associated with pregnancy, exhibiting a gradual rise in prevalence worldwide. Given the potential for numerous short- and long-term complications for both mother and child, patients diagnosed with GDM require individualised treatment to compensate for metabolic abnormalities and ultimately reduce the risk of the known adverse consequences of impaired glucose tolerance.

pmc-12578089.title: Engineering hope: tissue-engineered intestine as a breakthrough for pediatric short bowel syndrome
pmc-12578089.creator: Ayesha Khan, Maliha Khalid, Muhammad Talha, Aminath Waafira
pmc-12578089.description: Short bowel syndrome (SBS) in children, most often caused by necrotizing enterocolitis, volvulus, intestinal atresia, or gastroschisis, results in severe nutrient malabsorption and is associated with high morbidity. Tissue-engineered small intestine (TESI) offers a regenerative alternative to transplantation, circumventing organ scarcity and the need for lifelong immunosuppression.
